title: Formononetin attenuates corticosterone-induced depressive-like behaviors and neuronal damage via ERalpha/ERK-CREB-BDNF signaling pathway.
authors: Wang, Baoying; Liu, Hui; Zhang, Changjing; Yan, Xiangli; Xu, Erping; Bai, Ming; Li, Yucheng
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究芒柄花素通过ERalpha/ERK-CREB-BDNF通路抗抑郁作用，核心为小分子-蛋白信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Formononetin (FMN) is known for its significant neuroprotective effects, this study aims to investigate the antidepressant potential and underlying mechanisms of FMN. ‌METHODS: Antidepressant efficacy was evaluated in corticosterone (CORT)-induced depression models. In vivo, CORT-exposed mice received FMN to assess behavioral and hippocampal changes (dendritic spine density, synaptic markers: MAP-2/GAP-43). In silico, network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted FMN's binding affinity and enriched pathways. In vitro, HT22 cells pretreated with FMN (10 muM, 6 h) were subjected to CORT injury, with mechanistic validation via ERalpha antagonist (MPP) and ERK inhibitor (PD98059). KEY FINDINGS: FMN alleviated depressive-like behaviors and preserved hippocampal integrity in mice. Bioinformatics analysis revealed FMN's strong binding to ER subtypes and enrichment in estrogen/MAPK pathways. In vitro, FMN pretreatment activated the ERK-CREB-BDNF axis in CORT-injured HT22 cells, enhancing neuronal survival and synaptic function. The activation was ERalpha/ERK-dependent, as evidenced by the abolition of protective effects following pharmacological inhibition with MPP (ERalpha antagonist) or PD98059 (ERK inhibitor). Concomitantly, in vivo FMN treatment restored hippocampal p-ERK/ERK ratios in mice, directly corroborating the ERK-CREB-BDNF pathway activation and highlighting its efficacy in reversing CORT-induced signaling deficits. CONCLUSION: FMN exerts antidepressant effects via ERalpha-mediated neurotrophic signaling (ERK-CREB-BDNF), offering a mechanistic foundation for natural antidepressant development.
abstract_zh: 目的：芒柄花素（Formononetin, FMN）以其显著的神经保护作用而闻名，本研究旨在探讨FMN的抗抑郁潜力及其潜在机制。方法：在皮质酮（corticosterone, CORT）诱导的抑郁模型中评估抗抑郁疗效。体内实验中，暴露于CORT的小鼠接受FMN处理，以评估行为学及海马变化（树突棘密度、突触标志物：MAP-2/GAP-43）。在计算机模拟中，通过网络药理学和分子对接预测FMN的结合亲和力及富集通路。体外实验中，用FMN（10 μM，6小时）预处理的HT22细胞接受CORT损伤，并通过ERα拮抗剂（MPP）和ERK抑制剂（PD98059）进行机制验证。主要发现：FMN缓解了小鼠的抑郁样行为，并保持了海马完整性。生物信息学分析显示，FMN与ER亚型具有强结合力，并富集于雌激素/MAPK通路。体外实验中，FMN预处理在CORT损伤的HT22细胞中激活了ERK-CREB-BDNF轴，增强了神经元存活和突触功能。该激活依赖于ERα/ERK，证据是使用MPP（ERα拮抗剂）或PD98059（ERK抑制剂）进行药理学抑制后，保护效应被消除。同时，体内FMN处理恢复了小鼠海马中的p-ERK/ERK比值，直接证实了ERK-CREB-BDNF通路的激活，并强调了其在逆转CORT诱导的信号缺陷方面的有效性。结论：FMN通过ERα介导的神经营养信号（ERK-CREB-BDNF）发挥抗抑郁作用，为天然抗抑郁药物的开发提供了机制基础。
